name: cards
purpose: A collection shown as cards, after Cloudscape's cards: one card per item, named by its `header` slot, with the item's fields in the default slot. It shares Table's item and selection model — `items`, `trackBy`, `selectedKeys` — so `useCollection` binds it through `cardsProps`, and selection (single or multi, with a visible select-all) survives paging. Four cards a row in a wide container, then three, two and one as the container narrows.
useWhen: Items people recognise by a few fields or a picture rather than compare column by column (applications, templates, environments).
The card form of a list page (`platform/view/card-view`), filtered and paged by `useCollection`.
avoidWhen: Records compared, sorted or scanned across many fields → use `table`.
A fixed marketing grid of features or links → use `card-grid`.
related: use-collection` — filters, pages and selects; `cardsProps` is the binding.
table` — the same collection as rows; same item and selection model.
bestPractices: Put the item's name, as a link to the item, in the `header` slot: it also names the selection control.
Keep each card to a handful of label and value pairs; let `collection-preferences` choose which.
Use `selectionMode="multi"` only when a bulk action exists next to the list.

props.name: trackBy
props.doc: Field that identifies an item; selection keys read it.

props.name: selectionMode
props.doc: No selection, one card, or several cards with a select-all above them.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Shows placeholder cards and sets aria-busy while true.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog.

slots.name: header
slots.scope: { item: Record<string, unknown>; index: number; selected: boolean }
slots.notes: Card title; names the card and its selection control.

slots.name: default
slots.scope: { item: Record<string, unknown>; index: number; selected: boolean }

slots.name: empty
slots.notes: Shown when there are no items.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import Cards from '@aziontech/webkit/cards'
  import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'

  const applications = [
    {
      id: 'app-1',
      name: 'storefront',
      status: 'Active',
      domain: 'shop.example.com',
      requests: '1.2M'
    },
    {
      id: 'app-2',
      name: 'checkout',
      status: 'Active',
      domain: 'pay.example.com',
      requests: '310K'
    },
    { id: 'app-3', name: 'blog', status: 'Inactive', domain: 'blog.example.com', requests: '0' },
    { id: 'app-4', name: 'docs', status: 'Active', domain: 'docs.example.com', requests: '88K' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Cards :items="applications">
    <template #header="{ item }">{{ item.name }}</template>
    <template #default="{ item }">
      <dl class="grid grid-cols-[auto_1fr] gap-x-(--spacing-sm) gap-y-(--spacing-xxs)">
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Status</dt>
        <dd>
          <Tag
            :label="item.status"
            :severity="item.status === 'Active' ? 'success' : 'secondary'"
            size="small"
          />
        </dd>
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Domain</dt>
        <dd class="truncate">
          <bdi>{{ item.domain }}</bdi>
        </dd>
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Requests</dt>
        <dd class="tabular-nums">{{ item.requests }}</dd>
      </dl>
    </template>
  </Cards>
</template>
